task.description: REWORK re-implementation of ISS-0107 / GitHub #366 per the now-twice-revised, twice-validated design at src/design/fix-ISS-0107.md. Your original implementation (the widened bpm_test_migrations_public lock scope covering resetTestData()/applyCompatibilityShims(), still present in the current working tree at tests/integration/helpers.zig) correctly eliminated the original deadlock storm and does NOT need to change. What you need to ADD: bracket the advisory-lock acquire statement (currently at ~line 473: `try conn.exec("SELECT pg_advisory_lock(hashtext('bpm_test_migrations_public'))", &.{});`) with a plain sequential SET lock_timeout='90s' statement immediately before it, and a plain sequential SET lock_timeout='5s' statement immediately after the widened critical section completes (after applyCompatibilityShims(), before configureTestSearchPath() -- matching where the current unlock statement at ~line 505 already sits, so the restore likely belongs right around there). CRITICAL: use PLAIN SEQUENTIAL SET statements (try conn.exec(...)), NOT defer or errdefer for either the raise or the restore -- the design was reworked twice specifically to land on this exact mechanism (a defer-based restore would fire too late, after conn.begin(), leaving lock_timeout stuck at 90s into the per-test transaction). The existing errdefer conn.close() at ~line 431 already covers the failure-path cleanup concern (it discards the whole connection on any error), so no separate deferred timeout-restore is needed or wanted. Read the design doc's exact prose before implementing -- it specifies the precise placement and reasoning.
acceptance_criteria: lock_timeout is raised to 90s via plain SET immediately before the widened advisory-lock acquire, and restored to 5s via plain SET immediately after the widened critical section completes -- NOT via defer/errdefer for either statement
The original widened-lock-scope fix (covering resetTestData/applyCompatibilityShims) remains unchanged

zig build test-integration (full concurrent suite, run at least 2 times) shows: zero 40P01 deadlocks among the previously-colliding binaries AND zero (or negligible/unrelated) 55P03 lock-timeout-cancellation errors on the widened acquire specifically

TC-DB-01-01 and TC-DB-01-02 PASS end-to-end -- this is the original #357 acceptance bar; with ISS-0106 already merged and this rework addressing the 55P03 regression from the first ISS-0107 attempt, this should finally go green

Note: ISS-0108 (GitHub #368, a stray tenant_default.schema_migrations shadow table on the long-lived db_test container) was filed separately and is OUT OF SCOPE for this fix -- if you hit it again during verification, DROP TABLE tenant_default.schema_migrations manually to work around it for clean measurement (same workaround used during the first ISS-0107 attempt), do not fix it here

result.summary: Implemented design shape (B) exactly: added a plain sequential 'SET lock_timeout = ''90s''' immediately before the widened bpm_test_migrations_public advisory-lock acquire in TestHarness.init() (tests/integration/helpers.zig), and 'SET lock_timeout = ''5s''' immediately after the acquire succeeds and before configureTestSearchPath() runs. Neither statement is defer/errdefer-guarded, per the design's failure-path analysis (errdefer conn.close() at line 431 already discards the connection on any error; a function-scope defer would not fire until after conn.begin(), which would leave lock_timeout stuck at 90s into the per-test transaction). The already-implemented widened-lock-scope fix (commit 5f25d99) was left completely unchanged. zig build and zig build test both pass (exit 0) -- zig build test required correcting a stale BPM_TEST_DB_URL env var (was pointing at port 5433; corrected to port 5434, the actual db_test container port, per docker-compose ps). 2 full zig build test-integration runs performed, each preceded by dropping the recurring tenant_default.schema_migrations shadow table (ISS-0108 workaround). RESULT: this fix's own acceptance criteria are met in both runs -- 0 occurrences of 40P01/'deadlock detected' in either run (unregressed from the widened-lock fix), and 0 occurrences of 55P03 anywhere in helpers.zig's line-470s acquire region in either run (confirmed via direct substring search against both cleaned logs). Each run surfaced exactly 1 unrelated 55P03 (row-level lock in tests/integration/sch02_timer_polling_test.zig, pre-existing business logic, not this fix's acquire). Run 1: 92 failed / 544 passed / 645 total (9 skipped). Run 2: 82 failed / 573 passed / 664 total (9 skipped) -- both improvements over the original 103-failed baseline and the first ISS-0107 attempt's 3 runs. TC-DB-01-01/TC-DB-01-02 still did NOT pass in either run, but via neither 40P01 nor 55P03-at-the-widened-acquire -- both runs instead reproduced the separate, already-filed, already-out-of-scope ISS-0108 (GitHub #368: unqualified schema_migrations reference resolving to a recurring empty tenant_default.schema_migrations shadow table). New evidence gathered during this verification (the shadow table is recreated mid-run by a concurrent sibling's tenant-schema provisioning, not just present once historically; TC-DB-01-01's table-list assertion also checks 4 tables that migration GBL-073 intentionally relocated out of public) was appended to docs/issues/ISS-0108.json.additional_evidence_rework1 and posted as a GitHub comment on #368. Full detail in docs/issues/ISS-0107.json.verification_result_rework1.
